p: Ahaz the son of Jotham king: This was a wicked son of a godly father, as of him again came godly Hezekiah, and of him wicked Manasseh, save that God in the end showed him mercy. Thus we see how uncertain it is to depend on the dignity of our fathers.
pass through the fire: That is, offered him to Molech or made him pass between two fires, as the manner of the Gentiles was, Le 18:21, De 18:10.
him: For the Lord preserved the city and his people for the sake of his promise made to David.
Elath to Syria: Which Azariah had taken from the Syrians and fortified, 2Ki 14:22.
messengers to Tiglathpileser king of Assyria: Contrary to the admonition of the prophet Isaiah, Isa 7:4.
house of the LORD: Thus he did not spare the temple of God from being spoiled to gain help from men and would not once lift his heart to God to desire his help or hear his prophet's counsel.
according to all that king Ahaz: We see that there is no prince so wicked that he cannot find liars and false ministers to serve his purposes.

thereon: Either offerings for peace or prosperity, or thanksgiving as in Le 3:1 or else meaning the morning and evening offering, Ex 29:38, Nu 28:3 and thus he contemned the means and the altar which God had commanded by Solomon, to serve God after his own fantasy.
north side of the altar: That is, at the right hand, as men went into the temple.
brasen altar shall be for me: Here he establishes by commandment his own wicked proceedings, and abolishes the commandment and ordinance of God.
covert for the sabbath that they: Or tent, in which they lay on the sabbath, who had served their week in the temple and so departed home.

for the king of Assyria: Either to flatter the king of Assyria, when he should thus see him change the ordinance of God or else that the temple might be a refuge for him if the king should suddenly assault his house.
